#!/bin/sh
# Launch the TShock Terraria server non-interactively as a direct child of the
# supervisor. The upstream image's bootstrap.sh (a) drops into an interactive
# world-selection prompt when no world config is present — which hangs forever
# with the supervisor's null stdin — and (b) runs the server without `exec`, so a
# SIGTERM would hit the shell, not the server. This wrapper fixes both: it seeds a
# server config that autocreates a world on first boot, then `exec`s the server so
# the supervisor's stop/restart signals reach it directly.
#

content.text:
Your Terraria server is back up and players can join again. Your existing world loaded, so no progress was lost.

**What was wrong:** The server's config file (`serverconfig.txt`) had been edited so the world path read `Grizzly.wld` with a capital **G**. The actual world file is `grizzly.wld`, all lowercase. Linux treats capitals as different letters in file names, so the server couldn't find the world. It crashed a few seconds into every launch and kept restarting, which is why the bot only ever showed "starting."

**What I did:**
- Saved a copy of the config as `serverconfig.txt.before-fix`, then changed the world path back to the lowercase `grizzly.wld`. I didn't change any other settings.
- Restarted the server. It loaded the world, began listening on port 7777, and saved and backed up the world normally. A player connection came in during my check, and there have been no crashes since the fix.

**Two things to know:**
- If you edit `serverconfig.txt` again, keep the world file name all lowercase.
- When the server started, TShock showed a one-time setup code: `/setup 373105`. If you haven't set up your admin account yet, join the game and type that command to claim admin rights.
